competencies.text: Demonstrate how the Philippine archipelago was formed.

days.title: How the Philippines Formed
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

By the end of today's lesson, you will be able to explain the theory of plate tectonics, describe the geological processes that formed the Philippine archipelago, and identify the tectonic plates that interact beneath the Philippines.

🌏 The Theory of Plate Tectonics

Earth's outer shell (the lithosphere) is broken into large, rigid slabs called tectonic plates that float on the semi-molten asthenosphere below. These plates move a few centimeters per year — about the speed your fingernails grow.

There are 7 major plates and dozens of minor ones. The Philippines sits at the boundary of several plates, making it geologically active.

🧩 The Plates Around the Philippines

PlateDirectionRole in PH Geology
Philippine Sea PlateMoves westwardSubducts under Luzon and Visayas — creates volcanoes and trenches
Eurasian PlateMoves southeastCollides with the Philippines along western Luzon and Palawan
Indo-Australian PlateMoves northSubducts along the Mindanao trench — volcanic arcs in Mindanao
Sunda PlateMoves eastInteracts near Palawan and Sulu

🔥 Three Types of Plate Boundaries

Boundary TypeWhat HappensPH Example
Convergent (destructive)Plates collide; one subducts under the other → volcanoes, trenches, earthquakesPhilippine Trench (east); Manila Trench (west)
Divergent (constructive)Plates move apart; magma rises to form new crustMid-ocean ridges (not in PH, but e.g., Mid-Atlantic Ridge)
Transform (conservative)Plates slide past each other → earthquakes (no volcanoes)Philippine Fault System

🏝️ How the Philippine Archipelago Was Formed

The Philippines is NOT a single landmass that broke apart. Instead, it was assembled over millions of years through several tectonic processes:

  1. Subduction: Oceanic plates (Philippine Sea, Indo-Australian) sank beneath other plates, melting and creating magma.
  2. Volcanic arcs: That magma rose to form chains of volcanic islands (e.g., Batanes, Babuyan, parts of Luzon, the Bicol volcanoes).
  3. Continental collision: Fragments of continental crust (like the Palawan micro-continent) collided and attached to the growing islands.
  4. Accretion of terranes: Small blocks of crust — terranes — from different origins were added piece by piece.
  5. Faulting and uplift: Fault movements pushed some areas up (mountains) and dropped others (basins, seas).
  6. Sea-level changes: During ice ages, sea levels dropped, connecting islands via land bridges (this is how some species migrated).

🗺️ The Major Geological Features of the Philippines

FeatureDescription
Philippine TrenchDeep ocean trench east of Mindanao — up to 10,540 m deep
Manila TrenchWest of Luzon — site of subduction and earthquake risk
Philippine Fault SystemMajor transform fault running through Luzon to Mindanao — source of large earthquakes
Bicol Volcanic ArcChain of volcanoes including Mayon, Bulusan, Iriga
Mindanao Volcanic ArcVolcanoes like Apo, Matutum, Hibok-Hibok
Palawan Micro-continentContinental crust fragment from ancient Gondwana

🌋 Evidence of Formation

  • Volcanoes: Over 300 volcanoes, about 24 active — proof of ongoing subduction.
  • Earthquakes: The Philippines experiences thousands of earthquakes yearly — the Ring of Fire.
  • Fossils: Marine fossils found in mountains show that land was once underwater and uplifted.
  • Rock types: Igneous rocks (from volcanoes), sedimentary rocks (from ocean floors), and metamorphic rocks — all present.

🌏 The Ring of Fire

The Philippines is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire — a 40,000 km horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific Ocean where 75% of the world's volcanoes and 90% of its earthquakes occur.

📌 Quick Check

  • What is plate tectonics? (Answer: the theory that Earth's lithosphere is broken into moving plates)
  • What are the three types of plate boundaries? (Answer: convergent, divergent, transform)
  • Why does the Philippines have so many volcanoes? (Answer: it sits at the boundary of several subducting plates)

days.title: Match Game — Tectonic Features
days.content:
🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each tectonic concept or feature to its correct description. There are 8 pairs and unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

match.right: Theory that Earth's lithosphere is broken into moving plates
Plates collide; one subducts → volcanoes, trenches, earthquakes
Plates move apart; magma rises to form new crust
Plates slide past each other → earthquakes, no volcanoes

Transform fault running through Luzon to Mindanao

days.title: Scenario Challenge — Plate Boundaries
days.content:
🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Read each scenario and choose the best reasoning. There are 5 scenarios. You have unlimited retakes to reach 75%.

scenario.text: 🌋 Mount Mayon in Albay has erupted dozens of times in the last 500 years. Why is it so active?

choices.label: A) It sits above a subduction zone where the Philippine Sea Plate sinks beneath the Eurasian Plate, melting rock into magma
B) It has been struck by lightning many times
C) It is the tallest mountain in the Philippines
D) It rains a lot in Albay

scenario.text: 🧱 Scientists find marine fossils (shells of sea creatures) near the top of Mount Apo in Mindanao. What does this tell us?

choices.label: A) The area was once underwater and was later uplifted by tectonic forces
B) Fish used to fly
C) People carried the fossils up the mountain
D) The mountain was once a coral reef that stayed at sea level

scenario.text: 🌊 The Philippine Trench east of Mindanao is up to 10,540 meters deep. What causes this deep trench?

choices.label: A) The Philippine Sea Plate is subducting (sinking) beneath the Philippine Mobile Belt, pulling the ocean floor down
B) It was carved by a giant river
C) It's a dried-up volcanic crater
D) Coral reefs collapsed there

scenario.text: 🏝️ The Philippines is made of over 7,600 islands. Why is it an archipelago rather than a single landmass?

choices.label: A) The islands formed separately through volcanic arcs, collisions, and terrane accretion — and sea levels rose between them
B) An ancient earthquake split a single island into many
C) A comet struck the region and shattered it
D) Humans dug channels between the islands

scenario.text: 🌏 Why is the Philippines part of the Pacific Ring of Fire?

choices.label: A) It sits at the intersection of several tectonic plates, making it prone to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
B) It's the hottest country in the world
C) It has many active fires
D) It has the most tropical forests

days.title: Formative Check — Escape the Tectonics Lab
days.content:
🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Tectonics Lab

You have 3 lives and 6 keys to unlock. You need 75% (5 of 6) to pass. Take your time — read every option carefully.

escape.text: What is the theory that Earth's outer shell is broken into moving plates called?

choices.label: A) Plate tectonics
B) Continental drift
C) Big Bang theory
D) Rock cycle

escape.text: At which type of plate boundary do volcanoes MOST commonly form?

choices.label: A) Convergent boundary (subduction zones)
B) Divergent boundary only
C) Transform boundary
D) Volcanic islands form randomly

escape.text: The Philippine Fault System is an example of which plate boundary type?

choices.label: A) Transform (plates slide past each other)
B) Convergent
C) Divergent
D) Accretion

escape.text: How were the Philippine islands primarily formed?

choices.label: A) Through volcanic arcs, collisions, and tectonic uplift over millions of years
B) They were carried by the ocean current
C) They are fragments of the Moon
D) They were always a single big island

escape.text: What is the Pacific Ring of Fire?

choices.label: A) A horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific where most volcanoes and earthquakes occur
B) A ring of fire in Hawaii
C) A type of volcano
D) A boundary between continents

escape.text: Why are marine fossils found in Philippine mountains?

choices.label: A) The ocean once covered the area, and tectonic uplift raised the land above sea level
B) Fish used to live on land
C) People carried them up there
D) They fell from the sky
